title: Unit – 3 : Session – 8 : SLO – 1  |  Queue — Introduction
sections: A queue follows the FIFO (First-In-First-Out) principle.
In a queue, insertion is performed at the REAR end.
In a queue, deletion is performed at the FRONT end.
A SIMPLE (linear) queue is a linear data structure with a fixed size.
A CIRCULAR queue overcomes the limitation of fixed size by wrapping around.
A DEQUE (double-ended queue) allows insertion and deletion from both ends.
PRIORITY queue gives priority to elements based on certain criteria.
Queues are used in CPU (process/job) scheduling in operating systems.
In a queue, if the rear is just behind the front in a circular manner, the queue is said to be FULL.
An ARRAY (or linked list) is used to implement queues in programming languages like C.
The queue operation that checks whether it is full is called ISFULL.
The queue operation that checks whether it is empty is called ISEMPTY.
In breadth-first search (BFS) of a graph, A QUEUE is used to keep track of the next node to visit.
In printers, tasks are managed using a QUEUE to print in the order they arrive.
A queue where new elements are added based on priority rather than position is called a PRIORITY QUEUE.
